items.title: relink checks anchors and sweeps at the candidate base before writing
items.action: Issue 313. (1) plan_lock.relink gains a keyword-only, required parameter `vet: Callable[[str], List[str]]`. Right after `new, match = relink_target(repo, old, to)` and before `preflight`, `plan.base_commit = new`, `save`, the ledger entry and the tag, call `vet(new)`; a non-empty result raises `pd.PlanError(problems)`, so nothing is written. plan_lock stays free of plan_checks and history_paths, as it already takes `save` from the driver. Update the relink docstring to say the candidate is vetted first. (2) plan.py gains `relink_claim_problems(repo, plan_file, plan, candidate) -> List[str]` (under 15 lines, beside base_claim_problems): view = book_of(plan_file, plan).view() (cmd_relink loads the plan with pd.load_plan, whose item statuses on a receipts plan are all PENDING because the statuses live in receipts; only the book view knows which items are done); run pc.anchor_problems(view, repo, candidate) + pc.sweep_problems(view, repo, history_paths(active()), candidate) and return each as `at base <candidate[:7]>: <problem>`, the base_claim_problems shape. It runs on every relink, whether or not an item is done (D1A). (3) cmd_relink passes `vet=lambda sha: relink_claim_problems(repo, plan_file, plan, sha)` (or a functools.partial). (4) The module docstring's relink section (plan.py:132-136) and the --to help (plan.py:1109) say the candidate base must hold the plan's anchors and sweeps, else relink refuses with at-base problem lines and writes nothing. Copy the planned test file docs/plans/2024/tests/tests/scripts/test_plan_relink_check.py to tests/scripts/ first. Existing relink tests keep passing: their anchor (src/calc.py:1, def add) holds at every base.

anchors.expect: def relink(repo: Path, plan_file: Path, plan: pm.ActionPlan, to: Optional[str], save: Callable[[Path, pm.ActionPlan], object])
preflight(repo, tags) plan.base_commit = new save(plan_file, plan)
def cmd_relink(repo: Path, args: argparse.Namespace) -> int: plan_file = locate(repo, args.plan) plan = pd.load_plan(plan_file) entry, lines = pk.relink(repo, plan_file, plan, args.to, save)
return (plan.base_commit or None) if any(i.status in DONE for i in plan.items) else None

base = plan.base_commit if not base or claims_rev(plan) is not None: return [] found = (pc.anchor_problems(plan, repo, base) + pc.sweep_problems(plan, repo, history_paths(active()), base)) return [f"at base {base[:7]}: {p}" for p in found]
def book_of(plan_file: Path, plan: pm.ActionPlan) -> prt.RecordBook:
relink.add_argument("--to", metavar="REF", help="The new base (default: the patch-id match on HEAD).")

items.title: patch-id miss names the off-history end state instead of inviting --to
items.action: Per D3A. In plan_lock.relink_target, the refusal when fg.patch_id_match returns None keeps its first clause ('no commit on HEAD's history matches base <sha12> by patch-id') and replaces '; pass --to REF' with the end state, for example: '; a base squashed or merged away has no counterpart, and its off-history: warning in check is then the end state (--to only for a commit known to hold the base's code)'. strap_lock.py keeps its own hint (D4A). Copy docs/plans/2024/tests/tests/scripts/test_plan_relink_counterpart.py to tests/scripts/ first.

anchors.expect: found = fg.patch_id_match(repo, base) if found is None: raise pd.PlanError([f"no commit on HEAD's history matches base {base[:12]} by patch-id; " "pass --to REF"]) return found, "patch-id"
None when nothing matches, ``old`` has no patch id (a merge or an empty commit) or a git step fails.

items.title: Relink paragraph in the write-plan SKILL.md and README
items.action: Copy docs/plans/2024/tests/tests/skills/test_write_plan_relink_contract.py to tests/skills/ first. SKILL.md **Relink.** paragraph (step 8): after 'or takes `--to`', add that relink then runs the plan's anchors and sweeps at that candidate base (the claims `check` reads there once an item is done, and that a freeze requires there before one is) and refuses with `at base <sha7>:` problem lines when any fails, writing nothing. Close the paragraph with: a base squashed inside another pull request (or a merge commit) has no counterpart on HEAD's history; relink refuses it, and the `off-history:` warning is then the correct end state, so no `--to` is guessed. 'That is the cue to offer a relink' becomes the cue when a counterpart exists. README.md (the Locked paragraph, lines 67-69): append '; it refuses a base where the plan's anchors or sweeps fail, and a base squashed inside another pull request, which has no counterpart, stays off-history'. Keep both files clean for tests/lib/test_strap_lint.py (no first or second person).

anchors.expect: **Relink.** After the developer rebases or squashes, a plan base that left HEAD's history shows as `off-history:` in `check`.
After a rebase or squash moves the base off HEAD's history (`check` prints `off-history:`), `PLAN relink <id>` re-points `base_commit` on the developer's request and leaves the plan Frozen or Locked.

items.action: Bump plugins/harness/.claude-plugin/plugin.json version 0.78.0 -> 0.78.1 (patch: a fix, no new flag under D2A). The latest release tag is v0.7.0 and docs/RELEASES/v1.0.0.md is the proposed next release, so extend it: the Plugins table harness row becomes '| harness | 0.65.1 | 0.78.1 |', and the Changes list gains one line, e.g. '- Fix(write-plan): `plan.py relink` runs the plan's anchors and sweeps at the candidate base and refuses with `at base <sha7>:` problem lines before it writes the base, the `relink` entry or the tag; a base with no patch-id counterpart is refused with the `off-history:` end state instead of a `--to REF` hint (issue #313, plan 2024).' No other plugin changes.

commands.expect: the plugin.json version line and the harness row of the Plugins table

decisions.question: When does relink run the anchor and sweep check at the candidate base? check reads them at base_commit once an item is done (claims_rev, plan.py:351-357), and freeze requires them at the base while no item is done (base_claim_problems, plan.py:456-467).

options.summary: Always: a relinked base must satisfy both readers, so a base that breaks a later freeze --refreeze is refused as well as one that breaks check

Only when an item is done (claims_rev of the book view is not None), as issue 313 proposes; with no item done the relink writes unchecked and a later refreeze reports the problems through base_claim_problems

decisions.rationale: Developer choice 2026-11-17: always check. freeze requires the anchors at the base while no item is done, so a relinked base must satisfy both readers.

decisions.question: Does relink get an override flag that writes the base despite failing claims?

options.summary: No override: the refusal is final; a base with no valid counterpart stays off-history, which check only warns about

--force: write anyway and print each at-base problem as a warn: line; the plan then fails check until a write plus freeze --refreeze re-anchors it (unlock first on a Locked plan); adds a test and a minor harness bump

decisions.rationale: Developer choice 2026-11-17: no override. The anchors quote the old base, which its tag keeps reachable; off-history: only warns.

decisions.question: What does relink without --to print when patch-id finds no counterpart (a merge commit has no patch id, freeze_git.py:282-283)? Today it ends with 'pass --to REF', which invited the guessed --to in the plan 2023 incident.

options.summary: Reword: drop 'pass --to REF'; say a base squashed or merged away has no counterpart and its off-history: warning is the end state, and that --to is only for a commit known to hold the base's code
D3A plus the cause: name 'a merge commit has no patch id' when the base has two or more parents (git rev-list --parents -n 1); adds a test with a merge-commit base
Keep the message: TASK-1's check already refuses a bad --to; TASK-2 is dropped

decisions.rationale: Developer choice 2026-11-17: drop the --to hint and name the off-history: end state.

decisions.question: strap.py relink (strap_lock.py:465-483) has the same unchecked --to and the same 'pass --to REF' hint; a strap edit spec's base feeds its baseline SKILL.md (strap.py:706). Is it in scope?

options.summary: Plan relink only; file a TODO for strap relink (it has no anchors or sweeps to check)
Also make strap relink refuse a candidate base without the spec's SKILL.md (edit mode) and reword its patch-id hint; adds an item over strap_lock.py and strap.py

decisions.rationale: Developer choice 2026-11-17: plan relink only; strap relink is tracked separately.
